requirements.quote: The queue groups obligations as Overdue, Today, This week, Later, Undated, each group collapsible with a count, overdue first and sorted by age; group state persists per member.

Each row shows description, matter and case number, owner avatar, due label with relative text ('due Fri 23 Oct, 3 days'), kind icon, status and a Provenance Chip to the source line; overdue uses an icon plus text, not colour alone.
Closing an obligation always opens the close dialog requiring a reason (completed task, lawyer action, not applicable plus text); there is no one-tap silent close, including via swipe or keyboard.

On touch devices, swipe right opens 'Done' (which opens the close dialog) and swipe left opens 'Reschedule' (date picker plus mandatory reason); a visible button and keyboard shortcut provide the same actions.

Each item shows one drafted next step (task, reminder to the clerk, or letter to the client) as a collapsed card; 'Use' creates a task or an internal reminder immediately and a client letter as a draft that is never sent.
Filters (matter, owner, kind, source, group) and a text search narrow the queue within 100 ms client-side and are reflected in the URL.
Defects tab lists registry defects with cure-by dates and proceeding state; Certified copies tab shows applied, ready and collected with next action.
Reorder and group changes animate with layout animation (220 ms) and reduced motion disables them.

States: empty ('Nothing outstanding. Orders you confirm will add obligations here'), skeleton, error with retry, offline (read from cache; mutations queue and show 'Will sync'), permission-denied (viewer read-only, clerk without strategy text).
Keyboard: `j`/`k` move, `x` select, `d` done (dialog), `r` reschedule, `a` add, `o` open detail, `/` search, `g o` go to queue, `?` help; all are listed in the shortcut sheet.
Light and dark themes meet AA; visual baselines at 360, 768, 1280 px.
